subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit managed-service disable for `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM` override persisted generated service-env, state-dir `.env`, and config env values, or should those durable sources remain authoritative until edited?
rationale: Raw-stream logs can include prompts, tool output, and user data, so automation should not choose the sensitive logging precedence contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat unset, `0`, `false`, and `off` as authoritative managed-service disable signals, clear or override stale generated service env entries, and document the precedence.

options.title: Persisted Env Wins
options.body: Keep state-dir `.env` and config env as the durable source, and document that operators must edit those persisted values before a restart disables raw-stream logging.

options.title: Doctor-Guided Repair
options.body: Keep runtime precedence mostly unchanged but add status or doctor checks that warn and repair stale raw-stream service-env values before operators believe logging is off.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat unset, `0`, `false`, and `off` as authoritative managed-service disable signals, clear or override stale generated service env entries, and document the precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history in durable service-env helpers and is the clearest owner for the security-sensitive precedence decision.
